source: ICRA'13 Theorem 2 / STAR'13 Theorem 3 / TOR'16 Theorem 1 ('there is a bijection between its solutions ... and the integer maximum multiflow solutions')
flows: u(0) -> m1 -> m2 -> u(1) -blue-> u(1)'  (stay realised through the merge-split gadget)
finding: The flow->path map is surjective but not injective: a robot that waits at u can use either the green holdover arc or the gadget u(t)'->m1->m2->u(t+1). 'Bijection' is an overstatement (harmless for optimisation, but the gadget route costs 1 in c2 and blocks the edge). The Java compact model has no such duplicate (edge variables only for curV != nextV).
